facts.statement: Ambopteryx is a scansoriopterygid dinosaur from the Oxfordian stage of the Late Jurassic found in China.
facts.quote: Ambopteryx (meaning "both wing") is a genus of scansoriopterygid dinosaur from the Oxfordian stage of the Late Jurassic of China.

facts.statement: Ambopteryx is the second dinosaur known to possess both feathers and bat-like membranous wings.
facts.quote: It is the second dinosaur to be found with both feathers and bat-like membranous wings.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Ambopteryx is interpreted as either a sub-adult or an adult.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen is thought to be a sub-adult or adult.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Ambopteryx is estimated to have been 32 cm long and weighed 306 grams.
facts.quote: The specimen is estimated to have had a body length of 32 cm and a weight of 306 g.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen IVPP V24192 is an articulated, nearly complete skeleton with preserved soft tissue on slabs.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, IVPP V24192, is an articulated and nearly complete skeleton with associated soft tissue preserved on a slab and a counter slab.

facts.statement: The holotype was recovered in 2017 from the Haifanggou Formation near Wubaiding Village in Liaoning Province, China, and belongs to the Yanliao Biota.
facts.quote: It was recovered in 2017 from the stratigraphic equivalent of the Haifanggou Formation near Wubaiding Village in the Liaoning Province and belongs to the Yanliao Biota.

facts.statement: The head, neck, and shoulder regions of Ambopteryx were covered with dense layers of feathers.
facts.quote: The head, neck, and shoulder regions are covered with dense layers of feather.

facts.statement: Ambopteryx's forelimbs were about 1.3 times longer than its hindlimbs, with the ulna shorter than the humerus and nearly twice as wide as the radius.
facts.quote: The forelimbs of Ambopteryx were about 1.3 times longer than the hindlimbs, with the ulna being shorter than the humerus and almost twice as wide as the width of the radius.

facts.statement: The abdominal region of Ambopteryx contained gastroliths and large bone fragments.
facts.quote: The abdominal region of Ambopteryx contains a small number of gastroliths and large fragments of what appears to be bone.

facts.statement: Based on unusual dental morphology and stomach contents, Ambopteryx is suggested to have been omnivorous.
facts.quote: Previously, the diet of scansoriopterygids was unknown but their unusual dental morphology and the presence of gastroliths and possible bone fragments in Ambopteryx suggests they were omnivorous.

facts.statement: Ambopteryx is classified in the family Scansoriopterygidae.
Ambopteryx lived approximately 160 million years ago during the Late Jurassic Oxfordian stage in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: vivió hace aproximadamente 160 millones de años, a finales del período Jurásico en el Oxfordiense del Jurásico Superior en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: The genus name Ambopteryx derives from Latin and Greek words meaning "both" and "wing," referencing its membranous wings and bird-like body plan.
facts.quote: El nombre de género Ambopteryx se deriva de la palabra latina ambo que significa "ambos" y la palabra del griego antiguo πτέρυξ, pteryx, que significa "ala", una referencia a las alas membranosas del animal y al plano corporal similar a un pájaro.

facts.statement: The time range for Ambopteryx is estimated from 161.5 to 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Tithonian (161.5 to 143.1 million years ago)
